title: US Reportedly Detained and Released “El Chapo Isidro” in 2025, Semanario Zeta Says
author: Redacción/SinEmbargo
content:
_This article
by[Redacción/SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/redaccion/)
originally appeared in the [November 23, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4908796/eu-habria-detenido-al-chapo-
isidro-en-2025-lo-habria-liberado-dice-semanario-zeta/), a Mexican digital
news outlet._

_A document from the US District Court for the Southern District of California
indicates that "El Chapo Isidro" reportedly even appeared before US
authorities._

**Mexico City, November 23 (SinEmbargo).-** **Fausto Isidro Meza Flores,
alias["El Chapo Isidro"](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4908562/el-chapo-isidro-
enfrenta-su-primera-audiencia-desde-la-femdo-privada-y-via-remota/)**, leader
of the **Guasave Cartel** , was reportedly detained in the **United States
(US)** and subsequently released, according to an official document accessed
by _Semanario Zeta_ of Tijuana, Baja California.

The file in question was issued by the **US District Court for the Southern
District of California** , dated May 13, 2025, and concerns a motion to
"unseal" an investigation [against Fausto Isidro Meza
Flores](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4907509/la-captura-de-el-chapo-isidro-fue-a-
sangre-y-fuego-murieron-cuatro-de-infanteria/), as well as an arrest warrant.

> “The United States of America, through its legal counsel, asks the Court to
> issue an order lifting the seal [unsealing] on the indictment and arrest
> warrant in the above-captioned case," the document reads.

The file is signed by Southern District prosecutor Adam Gordon in San Diego,
and one of its paragraphs states:

> “The defendant has been arrested and has made his initial appearance in San
> Diego, California.”
>
> Court document cited by Semanario Zeta, May 13, 2025

In other words, he was in the custody of US authorities.

![Court document from the Southern District of California cited by Semanario
Zeta.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/chapo-isidro-
us-detention-2025-inline-1.jpg)Document from the US District Court for the
Southern District of California. Photo: Zeta.

> "The United States requests an order lifting the seal on the indictment and
> arrest warrant — solely with respect to defendant No. 1, Fausto Isidro Meza
> Flores — and that the attached redacted version of the indictment be entered
> into the court record," the document stated.

This would indicate that "El Chapo Isidro" was detained in the US in May 2025
and also appeared before a court.

Despite this, the drug lord was reportedly released, leading to his subsequent
capture on Mexican territory on November 20, when he was detained following an
operation carried out by federal forces in the state of Sinaloa.

## How “El Chapo Isidro” Was Captured in Mexico

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, “El Chapo Isidro,” could not go anywhere. Neither
could his people or his resistance units, made up of gunmen and supported by
armored vehicles and heavy weaponry. The Mexican Army knew where he put one
foot and where the other was headed. The elite of the Guasave Cartel, which
emerged as an offshoot of the Beltrán Leyva organization, had its days
numbered.

That is why, on November 20, when elite and regular forces surrounded him, his
ability to respond had been almost neutralized. Drones, planes, helicopters
and extensive intelligence work supported by the United States (US) gave the
operation certainty. When, for example, the criminals brought out their
.50-caliber weapons, the so-called “cop killers,” they were immediately
neutralized from the air. Despite this, nothing could prevent four infantry
soldiers from dying during the confrontation.

According to the Secretariat of National Defense (Defensa), the arrest
followed three months of tracking and data exchanges among Mexican
authorities, which made it possible to locate Meza Flores in Guasave, Sinaloa,
with intelligence support from the US government.

> "The US government’s participation was limited to exchanging information to
> pinpoint this person’s location and complemented all the work and effort
> that military intelligence agencies had been carrying out. It was done
> without violating any legal provision, and it also fully adhered to the
> principles governing the bilateral relationship with the United States:
> reciprocity, mutual trust, respect for sovereignty and coordination without
> subordination," the federal official clarified.
